lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed.

lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take up to two business days to show on your account.
lines.dispute_line: I understand, and I won't go into this product any further.

lines.restructure_line: I'll transfer you to our restructuring team, who can talk to you about that.

lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, that promise can't be changed on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our systems are not responding right now.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book that call back.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.

unsupported_rules: H: `no_promise` / `refused` is used when "no promise recorded and at least one product refused (F.4), the rest disputed or paid". This ranks refused above dispute and paid whatever the account order. The engine closes with the first product's ending instead.

H: `no_promise` / `service_error` is used for "G.6, or no promise recorded because of an F.5 failure". This ranks a create_promise failure as the closing reason when no promise was recorded. The engine closes with the first product's ending instead.

rules.too_much_skips_full.assumption: Saying the amount is too much does not make the agent skip later ladder steps that name the full amount. Only the next proposal becomes the floor.

assumptions: Wrong identity answers: the API ends the check after three wrong answers, but brief C.2 says the second wrong answer across both questions ends it. The brief is more specific, so max_wrong is 2.
Callback ask limit: the brief says 'after two tries', so callback.max_asks is 2. Confirmation limit: 'after two attempts you still cannot tell who is speaking', so confirm.max_asks is 2.
Opening wording: brief B.1 says 'This call is recorded.' The spec format allows the word 'recorded' only in the promise lines, so the opening uses 'We record this call.' instead.
Brief B.1 says to ask to speak with {first_name} {last_name}. There is no title variable, so confirm_ask uses the first and last name.
Opening question: the brief's wording is 'Can you pay the full overdue amount of EUR {amount} today?'. The engine's {amount} already says the currency, so 'EUR' is dropped to avoid saying it twice.

The opening question counts as proposal 1 (F.1), so opening_is_attempt is true and ladder step 1 is the opening question (full amount, today). Steps 2 to 4 are the F.2 steps: full amount on the deadline, 50% rounded up to the whole euro (never below the floor) on the deadline, and the floor on the deadline. Band attempts copy the brief's totals: Tier 1 has 2, Tier 2 has 3.

A step identical to an earlier proposal, the opening included, is skipped and not counted (F.3). Example: on the 15th the Tier 2 deadline is today, so 'full amount on the deadline' repeats the opening question and is skipped.

Tier 2 deadline: take the 15th of this month. If that is before today (not on today), roll to the 15th of next month. Only after that, move a non-business day forward. So roll_before_adjust is true and deadline_adjust is next_business_day.
Tier 1 deadline: the 6th business day after today, not counting today. This date is always a business day.
Overdraft floor: 25% of overdue_eur, rounded up to the whole euro (a whole result stays as it is). If overdue_eur is below 100, the floor is the whole overdue amount.
Card and loan floors come from the account fields min_due_eur and monthly_instalment_eur.
get_account gives amounts in euro and create_promise takes cents, so promise_scale is 100. No rounding is needed.
E.2: if the customer declines the floor after offering a lower amount, the agent treats it as a refusal of the current step.
Memo OPS-26-31 (dated): from 2026-11-04 the close reason for hardship becomes financial_difficulty. The add_note reason stays hardship. Calls before that date keep hardship.

The brief is silent on these, so the defaults apply: how 'next <weekday>' is read (following_week), max_not_talk 2, one 'anything else' turn after a recorded promise, and clamping a single date to each product's own deadline.
Brief C.1 says a spoken all-numeric date is read day, month, year, so date_order is dmy.
Notes are enabled: briefs F.4, F.5 and G.1 to G.3 require add_note for products that end without a promise.
No band covers days_past_due outside 1 to 60. The brief gives no rule for that, so bands_outside is omitted.
